evidence_quotes.two_concerns_question: NOT ASKED — Rep moved directly into logistics probing without the two-concerns frame.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — No concerns were raised by customer in step 2 because the question was never asked.
evidence_quotes.value_days: Rep identified Saturday the 17th as availability and quoted $230/hour for that day. When customer asked about Saturday availability mid-call, rep said 'Yes, we still have an available schedule on the seventeenth okay' but did NOT offer a cheaper alternative day as a total dollar saving or ask about date flexibility. Partial credit: value-day awareness but no comparative saving offered.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_then_ask: Rep said 'So, would you like to go ahead and get on the schedule today?' with no prior mention of rate lock or no-deposit guarantee. The ask was present but lacked the rate-lock framing that should precede it. Also, customer declined and rep did not push back or confirm details despite the soft no, suggesting weak follow-through on the ask itself.

top_strength: Excellent logistics gathering — Jevic walked through a detailed furniture list systematically (beds, dressers, desks, sectional, bar table, fridge), confirmed property details (one-story to two-story townhome, parking), and used that specificity to personalize a credible time estimate (3.5–4.5 hours for partial move vs. typical 6–8 hours).
coaching_note: Missing the two-concerns question entirely skipped the step 2 bookend and prevented any emotional connection to the customer's actual priorities; add the two-concerns frame before any logistics probing, then use their answers (not your assumptions) to drive the promises and estimate.
